blaine.tagline: Sarcasm, sourdough, and a Longhorn in-law situation.
blaine.backstory:
Runs coffee shops and bakeries in Dallas now, which is a respectable second act for a man who spent senior spring break in Panama City getting his upper ear pierced. The frosted tips are gone. The Timberlake energy never left.

He is the group's designated agitator — he will not argue with you, he will simply say one sarcastic thing and let it metabolize for six weeks. Married into Texas Longhorns. Has to sit at a Thanksgiving table full of them. This is the single funniest fact in the pool and he cannot escape it.
blaine.running_gag: The in-laws. Any Texas result is a Blaine result.
blaine.draft_tendency: Contrarian for the bit. Will take an under purely because you took the over.
blaine.fatal_flaw: Drafted special-teamers as his boys. On purpose. Repeatedly. And John Emery Jr. — a man who played approximately six years of college football and peaked as a 2019 freshman, which Blaine will tell you was simply early identification of talent.

chris.tagline: Radiologist. Podcaster. Two years in Paris and we'll never stop.
chris.backstory:
Shreveport-born, LSU-made, currently a radiologist in New Orleans by way of Nashville, DC, and — critically — Paris, France, where he lived for two years and from which he has never been allowed to return in our eyes. He is drawing on the storied tradition of French collegiate football, a tradition we invite him to describe at any time.

He is also a formerly elite Yelper, a man who made a genuine discipline out of reviewing restaurants, and he now hosts The Back Table, a podcast for radiologists, making him the pool's only working media personality. Through all of it he stays above the fray — says little, judges everything, and files a full review afterward.
chris.running_gag: France. The podcast. The Yelp reviews.
chris.draft_tendency: Measured. Doesn't chase. Will explain his reasoning like it's a chart read.
chris.fatal_flaw: Above the fray means unarmed when the fray comes for him.

jonathan.tagline: Builds spacecraft. Cannot pick a wide receiver.
jonathan.backstory:
Electrical engineer at NASA in Huntsville — the man works on the actual rocket. He is a genuine space nerd and the smartest person in this pool by a distance that isn't close. He also once played minor league baseball, a fact preserved for posterity by a baseball card of an unrelated middle-aged man who looks exactly like him, which we have used as his official portrait for years and will continue to use.

And then there are his boys. Drake — the one we all fell for, the one Jonathan claimed before anyone else could, the one who never gave us a thing. Jonathan Giles, Texas Tech's conference player of the year, who arrived in Baton Rouge, produced fourteen total yards, and has been Little Jonno ever since. Sevyn Banks, whose neck gave out on roughly the first snap of the season. Three blue-chip endorsements, three separate ways to lose.

The man can calculate a launch window to the second and cannot identify a wide receiver who will still be on the roster in November.
jonathan.running_gag: Little Jonno. Fourteen yards. Also the baseball card.
jonathan.fatal_flaw: His boys. It's a documented pattern at this point.

zach.tagline: Built the whole thing. Picked Marcus Randall.
zach.backstory:
Wake Forest, by way of Baton Rouge — went up to play soccer, didn't play soccer, came back a Demon Deacon with an LSU heart and a spreadsheet problem. He is the only man in this pool who will build a scoring engine, a projection model, a CI pipeline, and an AI art department for a bet you could settle with a handshake.

Twenty years ago he looked at Marcus Randall and called him the future of our team. Matt Mauck was standing right there. He has never lived it down and he never will, because he wrote the website that displays it.
zach.running_gag: “Future of our team.” Deployable on any pick that ages badly.
zach.draft_tendency: Overthinks it, then takes the number the model gave him anyway.
zach.fatal_flaw: Boys. Jack Bech, who we never threw to. Sage Ryan, five stars of nothing who left for Ole Miss.
